title: Секрет паштета  (The Secret of the Pâté)

segments.t: Barinov has led Max to the kitchen to show him what his famous pâté really contains. It is not what Max expected, and Eleonora Andreyevna, who loves the stuff, comes into it. We'll hear it in Russian first.
Let's look at it again, piece by piece.
'Beef pâté.' 'Beef' is an adjective here, so it's 'beefy pâté'. That is how Russian says 'beef pâté': one describing word and one noun.
'Absolutely revolting.' The first word is 'filth', and the second means 'terrible'. Together they work as 'extremely nasty'.
'But when you mix it all together...' 'If' is followed by the plain 'to mix', which gives it a general sense of 'if you mix'. 'All' has an 'o' at the end.
'Eleonora likes it.' Russian says 'to-her it-pleases', so the food does the pleasing. The little word for 'to her' takes the place of 'she'.
'Are you kidding me?' The 'sya' ending makes the verb 'mock' and means you are doing it to someone. Max uses the polite 'you' with the boss.
'Why?' One word again. Barinov is pretending to be surprised.
'You were educating yourself.' It's a made-up kind of word, built from 'self' plus 'bring up', plus 'sya'. Barinov enjoys the sound of it.
'Well, let's go.' The first word is the 'well' that Russians use when they change the subject. The second is the 'we' form, standing in for 'let's go'.
'By the way, it's good pâté.' 'By the way' is a single word. The 'good' has the masculine ending to go with the pâté.
'How do you make it?' Barinov uses the casual 'you', and the ending 'sh' shows it. He has gone from bossy to curious.
'What did you put in?' There's no word for 'you'. The question about 'did you add' relies on the 'l' ending, and the context.
'Beef, liver.' A list of two nouns, with no verb. Max replies with the plainest possible words. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.

So the famous pâté is a very ordinary recipe, and Max is left to digest it. You've now heard how Russians say 'by the way' and 'are you kidding me?', which will be handy for a lot of conversations. See you next time!
